author: cdc-rfc1-author (Claude Sonnet 5.5)
rationale: A unique reciprocal 4-phase handshake (req_q<-a2_q, ack_q<-r2_q) gives CDC-015 INFO plus a CDC-024 obligation; rx_q captures tx_q under synchronized r2_q, giving a CDC-039 stability obligation. RDC-023(b) is WARNING Unresolved for every recognized handshake whatever the reset kind, so the synchronous src_rst_ni/dst_rst_ni resets still produce it. Reader A's ack_q reset-during-request note is exactly the open RDC-023 reset-release obligation, so the case stays unknown.

author_reading.rationale: Four-phase request/acknowledge with a bundled payload: structure is recognizable but RTL cannot prove protocol sequencing or payload stability, so protocol obligations stay open.

labels.rationale: The request and acknowledge have reciprocal synchronized dependencies, and capture of tx_q requires r2_q. Payload stability, delivery, and reset coordination remain open.
labels.suspected_flaw: Resetting ack_q during an in-flight request while r2_q remains asserted can replay a capture. The contract does not specify whether that reset sequence is permitted.

labels.rationale: Structurally recognized 4-phase request/acknowledge handshake (req_q -> r1_q -> r2_q and ack_q -> a1_q -> a2_q) with synchronized-qualifier payload capture (rx_q <= tx_q under r2_q && !ack_q at design.sv:50). Structural analysis recognizes the handshake and qualifier necessity but leaves functional protocol correctness (CDC-024), payload stability during capture (CDC-039), and cross-domain reset release sequencing (RDC-023) as unproved obligations.
